analysis.title: JPM US Market Intel Morning Briefing, November 11, 2026
key_insights: Futures are rallying, led by Tech. Premarket SOXX is +5.2%, DRAM +8.0%, CRWV +14.6% and NVDA +5.2% on positive AI-theme news (CRWV, OpenAI, capital markets). The bond market is closed for the holiday, and cyclicals are leading defensives.

Hawkish CPI plus Fedspeak pushed yields higher and bear-flattened the curve (2Y +17.6bp, 10Y +10.8bp). Pricing for a 50bp Fed move in December is now 28bp, up 7bp from Monday's close. The terminal rate is 4.638% (Sept 2027) versus 4.404% on Monday.
US Market Intel reads the CPI-driven selloff as a reset of bond yields to match growth of about 3.4% in 26Q3. Combined with a robust earnings season, the desk is Tactically Bullish.

Monetization menu: the Tech washout appears at or near completion, though another Semis decline is still possible. The desk likes broad Tech and would consider US Memory and Semis via options. Moves may stay choppy if yields shift higher again.
The barbell of Tech plus Cyclicals makes sense, but the desk sees more upside in Cyclicals via European names and sectors than US ones, citing lower positioning and valuation.

On recession fears: the recession basket (JPRECES) is +14.9% since Sep 30 while SPX is -1.7%, NDX -8.8%, SOXX -22.7%. The desk calls the view that AI capex is the sole driver of US growth inaccurate. A drop in AI capex is unlikely to cause a recession because it added little to jobs, and consumers with large cash balances in a full-employment labor market remain the engine.

Feroli: nonresidential construction and related jobs tied to data center buildout are up 165,000 over the past year, only 0.1% of total employment. A policy-driven pullback in data center spending should have limited impact on job growth.
Feroli: professional, scientific and technical services jobs rose 33,000, a sign the feared AI job loss is still far off, though one month of establishment-survey data should not be over-read.

Fed view: the desk expects patience to see the effects of earlier hikes, US/Iran, Strait of Hormuz normalization and AI capex. 50bp in December seems premature but could change on a materially hotter PPI print. Feroli forecasts headline PPI +0.6% m/m (6.8% y/y) and core +0.4% m/m (5.1% y/y).

October CPI was hot again: core +0.30% m/m, headline +0.35%, versus JPM's 0.23% core forecast. The miss was concentrated in services (OER 0.32%, motor vehicle insurance 0.7%, recreation services 0.9%). JPM's core PCE forecast is 0.35% m/m, taking the year-over-year rate to 3.3%, the fastest since 2023.
Fedspeak: Waller backs a December hike and is open to 50bp. Logan says policy is accommodative, more rapid hikes may be needed this winter, and a pause would make sense after two more increases.

US Market Intel thinks the CPI print is unlikely to win support for a 50bp hike in December, given US/Iran resolution lowering commodity prices and lower AI capex reducing inflation pressure. The desk stays constructive on equities and prefers US ex-AI over AI into next week's capital markets event. Lower energy prices should keep the EU outperforming the US.

Lupton: the narrative of AI-led growth without jobs is not sustainable. The productivity boom reflects capital deepening and factor utilization more than technology gains. This supports JPM's call for a cyclical rise in hiring, sticky inflation and higher rates.

Small Business Survey: the hiring sub-index rose again (it leads NFP by 1-3 months), 86% of hiring owners report few or no qualified applicants, 37% plan to raise prices (highest since July 2022), and compensation is above historical averages. Credit is tightening and borrowing is below average.
Dubravko reiterates a YE26 SPX target of 8,000 on $365 EPS at 21.9x, which implies 8.4% upside from Friday's close.

Dubravko's trade ideas: long 12M Momentum versus short 3M Momentum (Tech versus Energy and Defensives), Low Vol less compelling (best in Healthcare, then Utilities, then Staples), AI Upstream attractive after the positioning flush, and Consumer Cyclicals challenged on affordability.

Dubravko attributes the pullback to a de-leveraging event. Investors held record leverage in AI plays, liquidity thinned from late June, and systematic and vol strategies plus buyside liquidations amplified it. October was the largest single-month Long Momentum unwind, about -11% or 6 standard deviations.

Dubravko says equity multiples compressed about 4x since January, an extreme de-rating outside recessions. AI multiples fell about 35% since May (Semis 52%, hyperscalers 14%, Memory 60%, Processing Units 50%).

On how much selling is left: Momentum crowding reset from the 100th to the 76th percentile, levered ETF selling of about $60bn Thursday and $35bn the prior Friday has cut exposure below Jan 2026 levels, CTAs flipped net short with maybe $50bn left to sell, dealer gamma is at the 12th percentile, $1.2T of announced buybacks should help, and QQQ RSI below 30 has averaged a roughly 4% rally over five days.

Dubravko's catalysts: Middle East developments, MegaCap IPOs, next month's ERCOT meeting (AI capex implications) and the December Fed meeting. He sees the US midterms as a clearing event and data center headwinds as less onerous than priced.

Dubravko estimates each $100B of AI capex adds about $9 to 2027 S&P 500 EPS (about 2.5% growth). Capex at about $1.5T would add roughly $18 versus consensus, or 4-5% to 2027 EPS growth. JPM credit analysts expect hyperscalers to fund 2026 capex absent shocks, but the funding mix needs more equity.
Looking to 2027, JPM Economics expects US GDP growth to slow but stay trend-like with modest disinflation, while Dubravko's team estimates EPS growth of about 20%.
Ex-US: Europe is higher (SX5E +0.8%, DAX +0.7%) with AI themes and Momentum/Beta leading. In Asia, KOSPI is +2.6%, NKY +1.3% and HSI -1.0%.
